summary: The article surveys how labor market policies are being used worldwide after September 2023 to create durable jobs and support sustainable growth. It covers reforms, youth employment, technology and automation, inclusivity, gig and seasonal work, globalization, human capital investment and fiscal policy, with country examples from Kenya, the EU, Singapore, Canada, the US, Mexico and France. It concludes that successful policies are proactive and defined by flexibility, inclusivity and resilience.
one_line: Overview of global labor market policy reforms since late 2023 and their effect on job creation, youth work, technology, inclusion and fiscal support.
key_facts: In October 2023 Kenyan Minister of Labor Elizabeth Mwangi spearheaded a labor reform that reduced barriers for entry-level workers and created thousands of new formal-sector jobs.
On November 15, 2023, the European Youth Employment Initiative, led by Commissioner for Employment Maria Schmidt, reported 250,000 youth jobs created through its apprenticeship program.
On September 30, 2023, Singapore's Minister of Manpower Tan Chuan-Jin announced a technology adaptation program that reskilled over 10,000 workers for a digital economy.
On December 5, 2023, Canadian Minister James Lee introduced the 'Workplace Equality Act' to stamp out discrimination and ensure fair employment practices across all industries.
On January 10, 2024, the United States Department of Labor launched a nationwide program to integrate gig workers into the formal economy while keeping gig flexibility.
On February 22, 2024, Mexican Secretary of Economy Carlos Salazar revealed strategies, following a landmark trade agreement, to make foreign companies adhere to labor standards.
On March 31, 2024, French President Emmanuel Macron announced the 'Education for Employment' initiative to reform higher education and close the skills gap.
Labor reforms range from reducing non-wage labor costs to enhancing labor market flexibility, and use fiscal stimulus for green technology, healthcare and digital infrastructure.
Youth entrepreneurship is encouraged through startup grants and mentorship programs, which also drive economic diversification.
Policies for seasonal and gig workers include improved social protection, off-season training and paths to permanent roles.
Fiscal tools for employment generation include tax incentives for hiring, subsidies for high-growth industries and public infrastructure investment.
Inclusivity policies target differently-abled individuals, the elderly and minority groups, who have historically been on the fringes of the labor market.
